newsitem.title: UK: Sixth person dies in British food poisoning case.
newsitem.headline: Sixth person dies in British food poisoning case.

text.p: A sixth person died on Tuesday in an outbreak of E coli food poisoning traced to an award-winning Scottish butcher, health authorities said.
The 72-year-old woman died after spending more than a week in hospital, the Lanarkshire Health Board said in a statement.
The other five victims who died last week were also elderly, hospital officials said.
The health board said 240 people reported food poisoning symptoms and 114 of these cases had been confirmed. Four children are undergoing kidney dialysis in a Glasgow hospital.
The organism responsible is E coli, a common gut bacteria that normally is harmless. But a toxic strain that lives in cattle can be passed to humans via manure or improper slaughtering.
It can cause sudden kidney failure, permanent brain damage and death, especially in young children or the elderly.

Some of the Scottish victims had eaten steak pie from a butcher's shop in Wishaw. It had supplied cooked meat to more than 30 wholesale and retail food outlets in the region and officials urged people to avoid cooked meat from those stores.

Recent outbreaks of E coli poisoning have been reported in the United States and Japan. More than 20 cases in Washington state, Colorado, California and Canada were linked to unpasteurised apple juice.
In 1993, 500 people became ill in the Seattle area and three children died after eating undercooked hamburgers.
In Tokyo last July, 11 people, mainly schoolchildren, died and 9,500 became ill from the bug.
